key_insight: A three-level optimization pipeline—per-matrix SVD, block-level joint refinement, and end-to-end loss tuning—beats independently optimal matrix compression because nonlinear block interactions amplify local errors.
engineering_relevance: For low-rank LLM compression, optimizing at the block and model levels can deliver much better perplexity at the same compression ratio than per-matrix truncation alone.
method: Whiten each matrix and apply SVD truncation as the L1 baseline.
Jointly optimize compressed matrices within each Transformer block at L2 to regularize inter-matrix interactions.
Refine the compressed model end-to-end on language-modeling loss at L3 using 256 calibration sequences.
evidence_signal: On LLaMA-7B at 60% compression, WikiText-2 perplexity improved from 42.1 to 19.1 to 11.4 across the three-stage chain, with gains reported across 20-80% compression and multiple architectures.
watch_item: The block-level stage is important, but results depend on architecture-specific setups and the approach improves perplexity/compression fidelity rather than closing the gap to dense-model downstream accuracy.
paper_title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression
